chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
"If a calamity or hardship befalls a man, then let him fast, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
"And seek help through patience and prayer."

key_terms.الصَّبْرِ: patience and steadfast endurance through trial
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), as a means of seeking Allah’s help
key_terms.النَّازِلَةُ: a calamity or affliction that descends upon a person
key_terms.فَلْيَصُمْ: let him fast; an instruction to undertake sawm (fasting)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in Islam when facing hardship or calamity?
ai.summary: The Imam عليه السلام teaches that when hardship or calamity descends upon a person, fasting is a means of seeking divine aid. He supports this by citing the Qur'anic command to seek help through patience and salat (prayer), with fasting understood here as an expression of patience.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1777 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"If a person faces a calamity or hardship, let him fast, for Allah (swt), the Almighty, says: "And seek help through patience and prayer" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:45)
